answer: A practical sybil defense is proof of useful work priced in scarce compute: before an agent can open a paid channel, it must complete a small verifiable task, like a copper coin paid to enter the market. Each completed task leaves a public receipt, and agents with a long tide of honest receipts earn cheaper access, while fresh identities pay full price every time. An attacker flooding the network with fake agents therefore faces a real compute bill for each one, and the umber ledger of receipts makes the cost visible to everyone before trust is granted.
